text:
Sam Nguyen: quick sync — we need a low-risk path for per-tenant residency + cost-aware routing. we can't do full geo-active rewrite for Q1. thoughts?
Marta O'Leary: high level: customers want EU-only for PII. Ops wants predictable cost. propose: residency flag -> prefer-local routing -> fallback to nearest non-local, *but* prefer cheaper slot if latency delta < X ms.
Devon Chen: but prefer-cheaper-slot adds routing complexity. how do we avoid double-writes for stateful stuff (kv cache / session lease)?
Ira Patel: idea: routing policy: primary-local (only for writes that require residency), read-through cache allowed to be remote. use a write-gate in proxy that attaches `X-Residency: eu` and a short write-lease token.
Sam Nguyen: concrete example:
```
POST /v1/generate
X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1
X-Residency: tenant-eu
```
proxy checks local pool. if capacity low, two options: A) queue until local free (latency risk), B) route to fallback pool but mark as "escrowed write" requiring background reconciliation.
Marta O'Leary: product prefers B for availability but legal wants guarantees. could we make escrowed writes opt-in per tenant? default strict -> block or queue, customer can opt into degrade-to-availability.
Devon Chen: escrowed writes complicated but doable: tag responses with `residency_status` and emit audit log. reconciliation job will copy final write to resident store asynchronously and fail if copy can't be completed within TTL.
Ira Patel: we need idempotency keys and monotonic lease numbers so reconciliation is safe. also KV cache eviction must not leak PII. recommend encrypting cache keys with tenant-scoped KMS envelope.
Sam Nguyen: cost angle: add a routing weight that's a function: w = latency_penalty_ms + cost_multiplier * $/token. if weight_diff < threshold -> route cheaper. does that sound ok?
Devon Chen: math's fine but we must be able to explain to customers. expose per-request `route_reason` in response meta: `local`, `fallback-cheapest`, `fallback-legal-exempt`, etc.
Marta O'Leary: UI + billing: show customers when they used fallback and incremental cost savings/loss. legal signoff required for allowed fallback types.
ops-bot: [alert] rolling capacity check scheduled for eu-west-1 at 02:00 UTC — will prewarm if flagged tenants > 1000.
Ira Patel: prewarm approach: when tenant flagged residency and QPS rises, spin up reserved slots proactively using predictive scaler. also make prewarming idempotent and cancellable.
Devon Chen: implementation notes: change proxy to include 3-tuple routing decision: {region, reason, lease_token}. store tokens in central durable index (simple 7d TTL). reconciliation worker reads index.
Sam Nguyen: follow-ups: (1) draft API header + response meta (2) outline legal fallback opt-in UI (3) infra prewarm + scaler PR (4) run a tabletop with security/legal.
Marta O'Leary: +1, I'll own opt-in. Sam, can you schedule tabletop with @Ira and @Devon? :calendar:
Sam Nguyen: will do. thanks. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy notice — background-worker v1.3 scheduled to deploy to us-east-1 in 3h (no eu changes).
